matches.gold_text: The program should serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority given to applicants that serve more than 400 participants.
Over 50% of program participants should be low-income.
The majority of program graduates should secure paid internships or full-time employment in AI or a closely related field.
Applicants must be organizations with a strong track record in workforce development in AI or similar fields.
If applicants form a team, one organization must be the lead for the proposed programming.

The extent of any cost matching should be indicated in the budget template.
Awarded applicants must track and record information relevant to the success of the grant, with data points determined during contract negotiation.

component_records.title: Bidder qualification and track-record evidence
component_records.description: The lead organization is a non-profit or for-profit entity that qualifies on its own record, and the proposal opens with the evidence ESD scores under Firm Qualifications and Experience. We document a quantified track record in workforce development in AI or closely related fields: length of training, number of participants served, number of cohorts, cost per student or participant, and internship and job placement rates for recent graduates, split between college-student programming and non-student high-tech training. We map that record against all four of ESD's domains (academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training, serving low-income populations, and work in the New York market) and show experience in at least three, with the fourth covered by a named partner where our own record is thinner. Where a domain is not applicable to us we say so explicitly rather than omitting it, so the Experience criterion is not lost by silence.

component_records.title: Program design, governance and ESD contract management
component_records.description: A single lead organization is designated as prime and stands up a program management office that owns the 18-month term, the monthly timeline from planning through first-cohort internship or job completion, and all ESD-facing governance. The PMO runs a monthly status and reporting cycle, a risk and issue log, a change-control procedure that asserts price or time claims within 30 days of written notification and keeps work going while claims are resolved, and a staff-change protocol that notifies ESD immediately and offers a substitute CV and interview before approval. It also holds the contract-level obligations: assignment restrictions, subcontractor disclosure and prior written approval for any subcontracting not named in the proposal, staff qualification and work-authorisation checks, professional-standards conformance with free correction of patent errors, and acceptance of Schedule A and OSC review conditions.

component_records.title: Curriculum, credentials and skill-attainment framework
component_records.description: We deliver an industry-informed online AI curriculum for both tracks, built with input from leading researchers and industry experts and reviewed each cohort against employer demand. Track A is a semester-aligned undergraduate pathway with real-world machine learning projects and mentorship; Track B is an accelerated bootcamp alternative to a degree, available part-time or full-time, with an immersive schedule. The component defines module-level learning outcomes, the skill-attainment metrics used to measure progress during training, the professional-development strand, and the credentials awarded on completion (with a stated position where no formal credential applies). Curriculum development is complete before the first cohort and refreshed between cohorts.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment, application and needs assessment
component_records.description: A targeted recruitment strategy reaches low-income New Yorkers underrepresented in tech who cannot reasonably access training on their own: campus partnerships and financial-aid offices for Track A, and workforce centres, community organizations, public-assistance and re-entry referral routes for Track B. The component delivers a single online application with a documented scoring and evaluation rubric, an income and eligibility verification step that applies one published low-income definition across both tracks, and a needs assessment that identifies each participant's barriers (childcare, transport, devices, connectivity, time) and routes them to the support that removes them. Recruitment is sized to exceed the 250-participant floor and to target more than 400 participants with over 50% low-income.

component_records.title: Training delivery, stipends and wrap-around supports
component_records.description: We run the cohorts: instruction, mentorship, project supervision, success coaching and career coaching with industry expertise, delivered online and scheduled to fit employer internship hiring cycles. Every enrolled participant receives a published stipend at a stated level and duration, plus wrap-around supports identified in the needs assessment. Attendance, engagement and skill-attainment data are captured in the learning platform each week so coaches can intervene early and so completion rates can be reported by low-income status. The component also carries the professional-development strand and the credential award at completion.

component_records.title: Employer partnerships, internships and job placement
component_records.description: An employer partnership function recruits and maintains relationships with leading New York tech employers, secures written commitments to paid internships and full-time roles, and feeds employer input back into curriculum content. For Track A we match students to paid internships that extend their AI skills through real-world work and networking and convert to full-time roles; for Track B we run full-time job connection support in AI and closely related fields, including interview preparation and employer introductions. Placement staff coordinate directly with each employer on requisitions, candidate slates and outcome confirmation, and we commit to a majority of graduates placed in AI or a closely related field.

component_records.title: Data, performance measurement and ESD reporting
component_records.description: A reporting platform captures the full data set ESD requires and makes it available on request: applicant, enrolment and completion counts with low-income percentages; paid internship and full-time placement rates with low-income percentages; participating colleges and universities; and participating employer partners. We add the three annual performance estimates ESD scores (participants served, low-income completion percentage, placement rate) with justification from our historical results and partner commitments, and we report against them each quarter. The data dictionary and reporting cadence are finalised with ESD at contract negotiation, and the platform is built to absorb additional fields without re-platforming.

component_records.title: Budget, price proposal and cost controls
component_records.description: We submit a line-by-line price proposal mapped to the 18-month program duration, with personnel services broken out by job title, named employee where known, hourly or annual rate, fringe rate, percentage of time and cost to contract, and each other-than-personnel-services cost on its own line with unit counts. The budget covers staff salary and benefits, wrap-around supports and the proposed stipend level, and curriculum development, marketing and events, with a written justification for every line. It is capped at $2M for one track and $4M for both, contains no indirect costs, and states the extent of any cost match in ESD's budget template so the match can be scored.

component_records.title: Diversity, MWBE/SDVOB participation and compliance reporting
component_records.description: We commit to the 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB participation goals and name the certified firms we will use, with the work each performs and the estimated dollars, on the OCSD-4 utilisation plans submitted with the proposal. The component covers the good faith effort evidence file (solicitations, responses, reasons for non-selection, meeting dates, scope-structuring steps), the quarterly MWBE compliance and payment report by the 10th day after quarter end, the monthly SDVOB compliance report on OCSD-6 by the 10th of each month, quarterly Workforce Utilization Reports including gross wages under Executive Order #162, and revised utilisation plans for any change. It also runs the seven- and five-business-day remedy and waiver sequence for any notice of deficiency, and the pre-waiver consultation with ESD's designated contacts.

component_records.title: Procurement integrity, certifications and insurance
component_records.description: A compliance workstream assembles the Administrative Proposal in ESD's required order: Non-Collusive Bidding Certification, Conflict of Interest Attestation, State Finance Law §§139-j/139-k forms and affirmations, Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire completed within one year, Iran Divestment Act Statement, EO-16 and EO-177 certifications, OCSD-1/2/4 diversity forms, NYS Businesses form, ST-220-CA and W-9. It also runs the conduct rules during the restricted period: contact only with the designated ESD contacts, no gifts or employment discussions with ESD staff, disclosure of actual or potential conflicts and of any ethics-commission investigations, and periodic updating of the 139-j/139-k disclosures during the term. Insurance is bound at award: $1M/$2M general liability, $1M auto, $1M sexual abuse and molestation, statutory workers' compensation and disability, ESD as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis, and waiver of subrogation.

component_records.title: Proposal assembly and submission
component_records.description: We build the response as a two-part folder structure with an Administrative Proposal subfolder and a Technical Proposal subfolder, named to ESD's convention and uploaded to the designated Dropbox before the 2:00 PM ET deadline, with no facsimile, hardcopy or email copies. The Technical Proposal carries a cover page, table of contents, bookmarked sections matching ESD's requested structure, firm and staff experience with quantified track records, one-page key-personnel resumes, employer partner letters, the Project Plan and monthly timeline, the Cost of Services section and the Diversity Practices Questionnaire. Questions are lodged by email to the designated address before the question deadline, and we monitor ESD's posted answers for clarifications.

items.text: ESD's Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) was created under Governor Hochul's April 2022 $350 million workforce development investment and is charged with aligning workforce efforts with employer needs and creating opportunities for unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented workers in the state's highest-growth sectors.
items.reason: All details are stated in S6.1.

items.text: ESD identifies AI as a high-growth sector advancing across healthcare, finance, transportation and manufacturing, and positions New York as an AI hub through institutions such as Cornell Tech and state-backed initiatives such as Empire AI.
items.reason: Sectors, Cornell Tech and Empire AI are all in S6.1; the high-growth identification follows from the text.

items.text: ESD's stated pain point is that rapid AI advancement may widen economic inequality because many well-paying AI jobs require specialized education and technical training that low-income individuals cannot access.
items.reason: Source says such jobs are 'often out of reach' and a concern; 'cannot access' overstates this, and 'pain point' is framed more strongly.

items.text: ESD states that tech company recruiting practices tend to favor students at elite schools and those with personal connections to prominent technology companies, which AI Prep is intended to counter.
items.reason: S7.1 states recruiting practices favor elite-school students and those with connections, and that AI Prep levels the field.

items.text: ESD currently has no AI Prep program administrator in place; it is seeking to award contracts to up to two qualified program administrators to develop curriculum and administer Track A and/or Track B.
items.reason: Seeking up to two administrators is supported; the claim that no administrator is currently in place is not stated.

items.text: ESD wants up to two program administrators to design and deliver AI Prep, an applied AI training program with two tracks: Track A (AI Prep 4 Internships) for low-income matriculating undergraduates and Track B (AI Prep 4 Jobs) for low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment.
items.reason: Two tracks, target populations and up to two administrators are stated in S7.1.

items.text: Track A requires the administrator to recruit low-income college students, run an application and needs-assessment process, deliver an industry-informed online AI curriculum with mentorship and real-world machine learning projects, pay stipends and wrap-around supports such as mentors and career coaches, and secure paid internships with leading New York tech companies leading to full-time jobs.
items.reason: 'Industry-informed' and 'full-time jobs' are supported, but 'requires' overstates. Internships are with leading NY State tech companies, as stated.

items.text: Track B requires an accelerated training or bootcamp alternative to degree programs, delivered part-time or full-time, with outreach to unemployed and underemployed New Yorkers, industry-informed online AI courses, stipends, success coaches, skill-attainment metrics, professional development, credentials where applicable, and full-time AI job placement support.
items.reason: Mostly supported, but 'accelerated training or bootcamp' comes from S7.1, not S9.1, and 'requires' overstates 'should include'.

items.text: The program must serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority for applicants proposing to serve more than 400, and over 50% of participants must be low-income.
items.reason: The 250 minimum, 400 priority and over 50% low-income figures are stated, but the source says 'should', not 'must'.

items.text: The contract term is up to 18 months, with possible renewal or extension based on performance, need and availability of funds, and the anticipated contract start date is January 1, 2026.
items.reason: 18-month term, renewal/extension basis, and January 1, 2026 start date all stated in sources.

items.text: Administrators must track and report data including applicant, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages, paid internship and full-time job placement rates, and participating colleges and employer partners, with the exact list set during contract negotiation.
items.reason: Data points and negotiation-determined list match S17.1; 'report' is minor paraphrase of track and make available.

items.text: Applicants must submit a budget mapped to the program duration covering staff salary and benefits, wrap-around supports and proposed participant stipend level, and other costs such as curriculum development, marketing and events.
items.reason: Budget components and mapping to program duration match S15.1.

items.text: Proposals are scored out of a maximum of 100 points by an ESD selection committee, allocated as Firm Qualifications 15, Experience 25, Project Plan 30, Cost of Services 20 and Diversity Practices 10.
items.reason: Max 100 points, committee, and each criterion's points are stated across the cited sources.

items.text: The Project Plan (30 points) must include a monthly timeline from planning through first-cohort internship or job completion, covering curriculum development, recruitment, training duration, cohort size, stipend level and placement, plus 1-page resumes of key personnel and employer partner letters committing to paid internships or full-time jobs.
items.reason: Timeline, activities, resumes, and employer letters all stated in S22.1.

items.text: Proposers must estimate annual performance against three metrics with justification from historical experience or partner commitments: total participants served annually, percentage of low-income participants completing the curriculum, and paid internship or full-time job placement rate of graduates.
items.reason: Three metrics and justification basis match S22.2.

items.text: The Experience criterion (25 points) requires quantified track records: length of training, number served, number of cohorts, cost per student or participant, and internship and job placement rates for recent graduates.
items.reason: Details are requested but not all required; college students section is 'if applicable'; Low-income and employer parts omit quantification.

items.text: Questions must be submitted by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov by August 29, 2025, with ESD responses posted by September 12, 2025, and proposals are due by 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025; late proposals will not be accepted.
items.reason: Email, dates, 2:00 PM ET deadline, and late-proposal rejection are all in sources.

items.text: ESD anticipates announcing the successful respondent on November 14, 2025, with interviews in the first week of November 2025 if necessary, and reserves the right to change any of these dates.
items.reason: Announcement date, interviews if necessary, and right to change dates stated in S18.1.

items.text: ESD reserves the right to conduct reference checks at its sole discretion and to use reference information in proposal evaluation.
items.reason: Sole discretion on reference checks and use in evaluation stated in S25.1.

items.text: Budgets exceeding $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks over the total contract period will not be considered, and indirect costs are not an allowable expense.
items.reason: Both the budget caps and the indirect cost exclusion are stated in the cited sources.

items.text: There is no cost-match requirement, but cost-matching earns additional points in scoring and must be indicated in the budget template.
items.reason: No cost match required, extra scoring points, and extent indicated in the budget template are all stated.

items.text: Applicants must be non-profit or for-profit entities with experience in at least three of four domains: academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training programs, serving low-income populations, and working in the New York market.
items.reason: Entity types and three-of-four domains match the source.

items.text: Proposals must be uploaded as a two-part folder structure (Administrative Proposal and Technical Proposal subfolders) to the Dropbox at https://www.dropbox.com/request/AIPrep; facsimile, hardcopy and email submissions will not be accepted.
items.reason: Folder structure, Dropbox link, and rejection of fax, hardcopy and email submissions are all stated.

items.text: The Administrative Proposal must include the Non-Collusive Bidding Certification, Conflict of Interest Attestation, State Finance Law §§139-j/139-k forms, Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire completed within one year of submission, Iran Divestment Act Statement, EO-16 and EO-177 certifications, OCSD-1/2/4 diversity forms, NYS Businesses form, ST-220-CA and a W-9, and failure to submit any may result in rejection.
items.reason: Sources don't say W-9 or each item is part of Administrative Proposal; ST-220-CA may be replaced by an affidavit.

items.text: The contract carries a 30% MWBE participation goal and a 6% SDVOB participation goal, with Utilization Plans (OCSD-4) required at proposal stage and quarterly MWBE and monthly SDVOB compliance reporting during the term.
items.reason: SDVOB plan is required with proposal, but MWBE plan timing isn't stated; the 30%/6% goals and reporting are supported.

items.text: The selected respondent must carry Commercial General Liability of $1M per occurrence and $2M aggregate, Commercial Auto of $1M, Sexual Abuse and Molestation insurance of $1M, and statutory Workers' Compensation and Disability coverage, naming ESD as additional insured with a waiver of subrogation.
items.reason: Insurance is required only 'to the extent applicable'. ESD must be additional insured only on CGL and Auto Liability policies.

items.text: Appendix A (ESD IT Security Standard Brief) and Appendix B (Diversity Practices Questionnaire) are referenced but their contents are not included in the RFP text, so bidders must obtain them separately.
items.reason: Appendix references are shown, but sources don't say contents are missing or that bidders must obtain them separately.

items.text: ESD requires applicants to be non-profit or for-profit entities with experience in at least three of four named domains.
items.reason: Matches the eligibility text exactly: non-profit or for-profit, at least three of four domains.

items.text: The Experience criterion is worth 25 of 100 points and requires quantified track records.
items.reason: 25 points is stated, but the 100-point total isn't in the source, and 'requires quantified track records' overstates the guidance.

items.reason: Intent to award up to two administrators is supported; 'currently no administrator in place' is not stated in the source.

items.text: The anticipated contract start date is 1 January 2026 and the initial term is up to 18 months.
items.reason: Start date is supported; 18 months is the funding period 'up to', not explicitly an 'initial term'.

items.reason: Source states recruiting favors elite-school students and connections, and AI Prep levels the playing field.

items.text: The exact list of data points is to be set during contract negotiation, so the reporting scope may expand after award.
items.reason: Exact list set in negotiation is stated; 'expand after award' is a mild inference, though list 'not limited to' supports it.

items.text: Budgets above $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks will not be considered, and indirect costs are not allowable.
items.reason: Both the budget caps and indirect cost exclusion are stated in the sources.

items.reason: 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB goals and monthly SDVOB reporting supported; quarterly MWBE reporting is not in cited sources.

items.text: The restricted period runs until approval of the Contract, and only the designated contacts may be approached about the procurement.
items.reason: Restricted period until approval of Contract is in S2.1; S39.1 says through final award and execution, but designated-contact limit is supported.

items.text: Questions are due 29 August 2025, answers are posted 12 September 2025, and proposals are due 2:00 PM ET on 1 October 2025.
items.reason: Dates and time are supported, but S30.1 does not state answers date; S18.1 does, so mostly supported. Fine detail fully present in S18.1.

items.text: One lead organization will bid for and deliver both tracks under a single contract, with the $4M both-track cap applying, rather than bidding one track at the $2M cap.
items.reason: Facts stated (up to two awards, tracks A and/or B, $2M/$4M caps) are accurate.

items.text: Low-income eligibility will be defined by the bidder using Pell-grant-style income thresholds with household-size adjustment, applied identically to both tracks and measured at enrolment for the over-50% test.
items.reason: Pell-based proposed definition and over-50% test are supported; household-size adjustment, identical across tracks, and measurement at enrolment are not stated.

items.text: Participant stipends are paid from the administrator's budget and internship wages are paid by host employers, with the stipend level and duration set by the bidder within the per-track cap.
items.reason: Stipends and the $2M per-track cap are stated; who pays internship wages and bidder-set stipend level/duration are not stated.

items.text: The program will be sized at approximately 400 participants across both tracks over the 18-month term, with cohort sizes set per track to fit that total and the budget caps.
items.reason: Minimum 250 participants, priority above 400, 18-month term and $2M/$4M caps are stated; sources leave total sizing open.

items.reason: 250 minimum and priority for over 400 are stated; the RFP does not say how 400 is scored, which the assumption resolves.

items.text: The lead organization will evidence its own record in at least three of ESD's four domains and rely on a named partner for the fourth, rather than claiming experience it cannot document.
items.reason: Three of four domains required; the partner for the fourth is the bidder's own position. Teams are allowed per S12.1 but not cited here.

items.text: The 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB goals are treated as commitments reflected in the submitted utilisation plans and priced into the budget, not merely good-faith aspirations.
items.reason: 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB goals are stated with good-faith documentation; sources are ambiguous about whether they are binding commitments.

items.reason: Equitable adjustment uses 'billing rates set forth in the contract'; price proposal is not mentioned in the cited source.

items.text: The bidder will obtain Appendix A (ESD IT Security Standard Brief) and Appendix B (Diversity Practices Questionnaire) separately and confirm that the security standards and questionnaire content match the scope assumed here before submission.
items.reason: Appendices A and B exist and B is required; sources do not say they are obtained separately or what Appendix A contains.

items.reason: Sources say not to provide Schedule A documentation with the proposal; Schedule A is not submitted, and not every listed item is clearly mandatory.

items.text: The 1 January 2026 start date is assumed to hold for planning purposes, with a 60-day mobilisation before first-cohort intake and a contingency in the timeline if OSC review or ESD date changes delay execution.
items.reason: The 1 January 2026 start date is anticipated, dates may change, and OSC approval may be required; the 60-day mobilisation is the bidder's own position.

items.text: The bidder will submit written concerns about Schedule A terms with the Administrative Proposal while withholding the Schedule A documentation itself, resolving the conflict between the two instructions.
items.reason: Concerns are to be submitted in writing with the Administrative Proposal and Schedule A documentation is not to be provided; the apparent conflict is ambiguous.

items.text: The bidder will include only the content ESD specifically requests in the Technical Proposal, with the Cost of Services section carrying the price detail rather than duplicating it elsewhere.
items.reason: Sources state no information is required beyond what is requested, and list Cost of Services as a Technical Proposal section.

items.text: Schedule A and Appendix B not in the RFP, yet both are mandatory. Schedule A (standard contract requirements) and Appendix B (Diversity Practices Questionnaire) are referenced but not included in the RFP, and Appendix B is worth 10 of the 100 scoring points. If the bidder cannot obtain them before the deadline, the Diversity Practices score is lost and the contract terms are accepted unseen. The bidder must also obtain Appendix A (IT Security Standard Brief) to know what security obligations the delivered platform must meet. Three referenced documents are absent from the PDF, and one of them (Appendix B) is a scored, mandatory submission item; the RFP gives no content for any of them.
items.reason: Appendix B is scored 10 points and mandatory, but sources don't show Schedule A/Appendices absent, 100 total points, or Appendix A security obligations.

items.text: Budget cap may not cover stipends, wrap-around supports and 400+ participants. The $2M per track / $4M both-track cap must absorb staff and fringe, participant stipends, wrap-around supports, curriculum development, marketing, events, MWBE/SDVOB subcontracting and compliance reporting, with no indirect costs allowed. The RFP does not say what share must go to stipends or how many participants are expected, so the bidder must choose between a stipend level that is too low to remove barriers and a participant count that cannot be served within the cap. If the arithmetic does not close, the bid is either non-responsive or loss-making. The cap is hard (over-cap budgets are not considered), indirect costs are barred, and the solution commits to exceeding 400 participants with stipends and wrap-around supports priced inside the same cap.
items.reason: Cap, no indirect costs, 400+ priority supported; MWBE/SDVOB subcontracting and compliance reporting costs, and 'commits to exceeding 400' not in sources.

items.text: Stipend and internship wage responsibility is undefined. The RFP does not say whether the administrator's budget or the host employers pay participant stipends and internship wages, nor the stipend amount or duration. The proposed solution assumes stipends come from the administrator's budget and internship wages from host employers. If ESD expects the administrator to fund internship wages as well, the per-track cap is breached; if employers are expected to pay stipends, the employer letters must say so. The assumption drives a large share of the price and rests on an inference, not on RFP text; the cap leaves no headroom if it is wrong.
items.reason: Stipends are administrator-provided and cap are stated; silence on wages and the solution's assumption not in sources, and employer letters context is unsupported.

items.text: 18-month term with a 60-day mobilisation leaves little room for placement outcomes. The contract starts on the anticipated 1 January 2026 and runs up to 18 months, and the solution spends the first 60 days on mobilisation before first-cohort intake. Training, paid internships and full-time placement for the first cohort must then fit inside the remaining term, and the scored performance estimates are annual. If OSC review or a late award pushes the start date, the placement phase is compressed or falls outside the term. The term is fixed at up to 18 months and the start date is only anticipated; the solution's own mobilisation consumes a tenth of the term before any participant is served.
items.reason: Start date, 18-month term and OSC approval are supported; the 60-day mobilisation and annual scoring consequences are not stated in sources.

items.text: Employer commitments to paid internships and jobs are not yet secured. The proposal must include letters from partner employers committing to paid internships or full-time employment, and the scored placement rate depends on those commitments. The solution assumes a partner network of New York colleges and employers will sign before submission and will deliver requisitions during the term. If letters are thin or employers withdraw, the Project Plan and Experience scores fall and the majority-placement commitment is at risk. Employer letters are a mandatory submission item and the placement outcome is a scored commitment, but the solution treats the network as an assumption rather than a secured asset.
items.reason: Employer letters and placement goal supported; 'scored placement rate', Experience score, and the solution's partner network assumption are not in sources.

items.text: Administrative forms are link-only and a missing one is fatal. The Administrative Proposal must contain a long list of certifications, forms and questionnaires in a prescribed order, most provided only by external link, and failure to submit any may result in rejection. The solution assumes every listed item is mandatory and will be obtained from ESD's links. A broken link, an outdated form version or a missing sub-consultant 139-j/139-k form would make the whole bid non-responsive. Roughly twenty separate forms are required, several are link-only, and the RFP states that omission may result in rejection; the solution's completeness depends on links the bidder does not control.
items.reason: Form list, order, rejection risk, and sub-consultant forms supported; 'roughly twenty forms' overstated (eleven items) and 'outdated version' unsupported.

items.text: Schedule A instructions contradict each other. The RFP tells respondents not to include Schedule A information or documentation in the proposal, but also requires them to review Schedule A and submit written concerns with the Administrative Proposal. A bidder that submits concerns risks being read as including Schedule A material; one that stays silent waives its objections to contract terms it has never seen. Either way the bid is exposed at contract negotiation. The two instructions are directly opposed and the underlying document is missing, so the bidder cannot resolve the conflict from the RFP text.
items.reason: Contradictory instructions and waiver supported; Schedule A being missing from the RFP is not shown, only a sample link.

items.text: Low-income definition and measurement point left to the bidder. The RFP does not define 'low-income' or say whether the over-50% test is measured at enrolment or completion, yet the bidder must propose its own definition and commit to annual performance estimates on low-income completion. The proposed solution adopts Pell-style thresholds measured at enrolment. If ESD applies a different definition or measures at completion, the recruitment targets, the support budget and the scored performance estimates all move. The definition is a scored commitment (R040, R098) and the RFP leaves it open; the solution's choice is an inference that ESD has not confirmed.
items.reason: RFP does define low-income as Pell-eligible with alternatives allowed, contradicting 'does not define'; measurement point ambiguity and metrics are supported.

items.text: Technical Proposal scope conflict: complete versus nothing extra. One requirement asks for a proposal that clearly and concisely provides all information requested; another forbids any information beyond what is specifically requested. The proposed solution resolves this by keeping price detail in the Cost of Services section only, but a strict reading could still penalise narrative that ESD considers extraneous, or penalise omissions where the RFP's requests are only 'if applicable'. The conflict is explicit in the RFP and the scoring weights (Project Plan 30, Experience 25) make both completeness and conformance material.
items.reason: Both instructions are supported; 'Project Plan 30, Experience 25' weights and 'if applicable' penalty claim are only partly in sources (Project Plan 30 only).

items.text: Reporting scope fixed only after award. The exact data points ESD will require are to be set during contract negotiation, so the reporting effort cannot be fully priced. The proposed solution builds a reporting platform and a data analyst role sized to the currently listed data points. If ESD adds fields, cohorts or cadence after award, the analyst capacity and platform work grow without a matching budget line. The RFP explicitly defers the data dictionary to negotiation, and the solution prices a fixed analyst role against an open scope.
items.reason: Deferral of data points to contract negotiation is supported; the platform, analyst role and pricing are about the proposed solution, which the sources don't cover.

items.text: OSC approval may delay contract execution. The contract is not valid or enforceable until the Office of the State Comptroller grants any required review and approval, and the RFP does not say whether this procurement will be subject to it. A multi-month OSC review would push the 1 January 2026 start, strand mobilisation costs and shorten the delivery window the price was built on. The RFP conditions validity on OSC approval but leaves it open whether approval is required for this award.
items.reason: OSC approval condition, the uncertainty over whether it applies, and the January 1, 2026 start date are all in the sources.

items.text: MWBE and SDVOB goals treated as firm commitments inside a capped budget. The solution commits to the 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB goals in the utilisation plans and prices them into the budget, with quarterly and monthly compliance reporting and liquidated damages for shortfalls. If certified firms cannot be found for the specific work at the price assumed, the bidder either misses the goal and faces damages or absorbs the cost inside the cap. Several of the governing forms and Schedule B are not in the RFP. The goals carry liquidated damages and payment withholding, the forms (OCSD-4, Schedule B) are missing from the RFP, and the budget cap leaves no margin for a premium on certified subcontractors.
items.reason: Goals, reporting and payment withholding are supported. Forms missing from the RFP and the budget cap are not in the sources, nor is the claim that liquidated damages apply to SDVOB shortfalls.
